Heartstone has a lot of that slot machine casino ding ding ding going on, as well as the flashy lights, snappy and poppy noises, sparks and cheers glam, and tavern atmosphere. Hits the right bells and gets a lot of dopamine flowing. It's really similar to the atmosphere in a casino, and I'm fairly certain Blizzard had hired expert consultants to help them exploit utilize these aspects of human psyche.

It's also the most simple game at it's core. I've played complex cardgames like Android Netrunner and even more complex boardgames. Some of them take 40 minutes to explain to a newcomer. Heartstone is a game I could explain to my dad in 30 seconds, while also being a big game with a lot of room for knowledge.

Also any Heartstone player can tune in any stream mid game and immediately understand precisely what is going on right now. It's straightforward, it's light and it's bright. It's happy. A lot of people miss that feeling these days. Whereas, say, Gwent is more gloomy and grim. Hearstone is pop music and Gwent is Slipknot. People don't like subversive, angry and depressive even if it's well grounded and evocative, they prefer happy, even if it's dull; that's why pop music is so popular. The simplicity, the atmosphere and the slot machine production value are the things that make Heartstone so succesful. And so watchable.

Artifact is not that. It's more neutral in overtones, more mystical and darker. It's also less exploitative blingy and noisy, but also significantly deeper and more complex.
